items.rationale: Glazing breakage is optional (2.1(e)) and the description does not say it was taken, so 2.6.4 and 3.5 exclude the pane. Case 3 shows the same line at t=0.
Drilling is glazing work under 1.3 and 3.5(b). The glazing peril is not agreed, so it is excluded, as in Case 3.

items.description: Installation of new glass into frame
items.rationale: Fitting the glass is glazing work (3.5(b)) and an ancillary charge following an uncovered principal item (7.1.11). t=0.
Removing and disposing of the broken element is part of the glazing work (3.5(b)), and 5.2.1 does not extend debris removal to non-covered damage. t=0.

items.description: Repair of dented solid-wood side table
items.rationale: Sudden accidental damage (2.6) to freestanding furniture is covered under the contents cover as an affected item. The repair is a fair market price for a dented solid-wood table, in line with the Case 3 timber frame repair.

items.description: Touch-up of pre-existing scratches on second cabinet
items.rationale: This is a pre-existing condition on an item the event did not damage (3.6(a), 7.1.9), as in the Case 2 lid scuff polish. t=0.

One attendance per undertaking is payable if indemnified work was done at that visit (7.1.12), and the side table repair qualifies. The charge is small, as in the reference cases where vehicle lines were low.
A return visit is not separately indemnified without prior insurer agreement (7.1.12). t=0.
General administrative charges on top of itemised labour are not repair costs (7.1.8(b)). t=0.
